results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response:
The types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain include [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [[Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), as well as alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into subtypes such as core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, and dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t classes, according to VFB. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") records of subclasses of Kenyon cell. 

To learn more about the different types of Kenyon cells, you can explore the available data in VFB, such as the list of available images of Kenyon cell, scRNAseq data for Kenyon cell, transgene expression in Kenyon cell, downstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell, and upstream connectivity classes for Kenyon cell.

results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. results.title: Circuit motif
results.question: Describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs). Which DAN types connect to which MBON types?
results.response:
To describe the dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and determine which types of dopaminergic neurons (DANs) connect to which types of MBONs, we can refer to the available data in VFB. 

VFB holds extensive data on both adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons and mushroom body output neurons (MBONs), including their subclasses, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) data, transgene expression, and connectivity classes. Specifically, for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons, VFB has annotated [21](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00049839,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") subclasses, [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00049839,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") scRNAseq datasets, [64](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00049839,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") transgene expressions, [316](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00049839,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") downstream connectivity classes, and [1290](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00049839,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") upstream connectivity classes. For MBONs, VFB contains [69](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of MBON") subclasses, [1](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for MBON") scRNAseq dataset, [157](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in MBON") transgene expressions, [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream connectivity classes, and [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes.

The upstream connectivity classes for MBONs include data that could indicate the types of neurons, including dopaminergic neurons, that provide input to MBONs. Similarly, the downstream connectivity classes for adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons could provide insights into which MBON types they connect to. However, without specific connectivity data between these neuron types in the provided evidence, the exact connections between specific types of DANs and MBONs cannot be determined from the information given.

To find the specific connections between types of dopaminergic neurons and MBONs, one would need to explore the detailed connectivity data available in VFB, particularly focusing on the upstream connectivity classes of MBONs and the downstream connectivity classes of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons. This exploration could reveal which types of DANs are presynaptic to which types of MBONs, based on the annotated connectivity data in VFB.

results.response: The LPLC2 visual neuron type is described as an adult visual projection neuron. According to the VFB database, it has a columnar arborization pattern. VFB records show that this neuron type connects multiple optic lobe neuropil domains, specifically the lobula, lobula plate, and medulla, and projects to the central brain. This information is based on a summary of the neuron profile available in VFB, which cites Otsuna and Ito, 2006. results.title: Bidirectional connectivity
results.question: Are there reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs)? Which pairs have the strongest mutual connectivity?
results.response: The connectome data indicates that there are reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons. The target-to-source weight is 7620 and the source-to-target weight is 2697. VFB holds a range of data on both dopaminergic neuron and mushroom body output neuron, including downstream and upstream connectivity classes, which may provide further insight into their connections. For example, VFB has annotated [8845](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") downstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron and [7914](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") upstream connectivity classes, as well as [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream and [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes for mushroom body output neuron. results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response:
To trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain"), we can refer to the information provided by VFB. According to VFB, a high-level pathway is [olfactory receptor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005926 "Open olfactory receptor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> adult lateral horn. The antennal lobe projection neuron is described as an interneuron whose dendrite innervates the antennal lobe and whose axon innervates some higher brain center, including the mushroom body calyx and/or the adult lateral horn.

VFB holds various data related to the olfactory receptor neuron and the adult lateral horn, including downstream and upstream connectivity classes, which may provide further insights into the connections between these neurons. For example, VFB has annotated [575](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron") downstream connectivity classes for the olfactory receptor neuron and [379](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron") upstream connectivity classes. Additionally, VFB has data on neurons with synaptic terminals in the adult lateral horn, which could be relevant for understanding the connections to this region.

The user can explore the available data in more detail by querying VFB for specific information, such as the images of olfactory receptor neurons, subclasses of olfactory receptor neurons, or neurons with some part in the adult lateral horn. VFB has annotated a large number of records related to these terms, including [19014](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of olfactory receptor neuron") images of olfactory receptor neurons, [92](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of olfactory receptor neuron") subclasses of olfactory receptor neurons, and [1661](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult lateral horn") neurons with some part in the adult lateral horn.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as noted by Thomas and Wyman (1984). According to VFB, it has a distinct anatomy and connectivity. VFB records show that the giant fiber neuron has a large descending axon. The cell body of the Drosophila DNp01 giant fiber neuron is located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, with one cell per hemisphere, as described by Koto et al. (1981) and Namiki et al. (2018). 

VFB holds [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of the DNp01 giant fiber neuron, [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01, [361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes for DNp01, and [435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes for DNp01. The connectome data indicates that the giant fiber neuron has specific downstream and upstream connectivity. 

Genetic tools associated with the giant fiber neuron include GAL4 driver lines, such as P{VT046265-GAL4}, which has a specific expression pattern. 

Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), and Namiki et al. (2018). Further information on the giant fiber neuron can be explored through VFB's available data and queries.
